intro: A young torchbearer for Louisiana Creole music.
story: Cedric Watson was born in 1983 and raised in San Felipe, Texas, then moved to Lafayette, Louisiana to learn zydeco and Creole music. He left the Pine Leaf Boys to form Bijou Creole in 2006, and his records drew Grammy nominations in the zydeco and Cajun category in 2009, 2010 and 2011. Le Troubadour Creole came out on his own Lache Pas label in 2013, the year he brought the band to Pickathon. They remain steady on the road and played the New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival in April 2026.
artist_reel_line: He played the New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival in April 2026.

intro: A theatrical psychedelic duo in a breakout year.
story: Foxygen are Sam France and Jonathan Rado, whose theatrical, 1960s-indebted psychedelic pop made 2013 a whirlwind year. We Are the 21st Century Ambassadors of Peace & Magic came out on Jagjaguwar in January, produced by Richard Swift after a week at his National Freedom studio, and they played Pickathon that summer. ...And Star Power followed in 2014 and Hang in 2017. The duo stepped back from touring after Seeing Other People in 2019.
artist_reel_line: They stepped back from touring after Seeing Other People in 2019.

story: King Tuff is Kyle Thomas, a Vermont songwriter whose fuzzy, hook-filled glam-garage anthems came to Pickathon in 2013, a year after his self-titled Sub Pop album, produced by Bobby Harlow. Black Moon Spell followed on Sub Pop in 2014, with Ty Segall contributing, and he returned to the farm in 2015. The Other came in 2018 and Smalltown Stardust in 2023, in gentler psych-folk textures. In late 2026 he played club dates with Sheer Mag.
artist_reel_line: He scheduled late-2026 club dates alongside Sheer Mag.

story: The Cactus Blossoms are the Minneapolis brothers Jack Torrey and Page Burkum, whose Everly-style blood harmonies were a Midwestern secret when they played Pickathon in 2012, and they returned in 2013 and again in 2025. After a 2011 debut and Live at the Turb Club in 2013, they signed to Red House, which put out You're Dreaming in 2016, produced by JD McPherson. They later started their own label, Easy Way, and toured the Southwest and California in late 2026.
artist_reel_line: They run their own label, Easy Way, and toured the Southwest in late 2026.

intro: An indie icon whose songs leave space for listening.
story: Feist, first known from Broken Social Scene, was already an international indie name when she played Pickathon in 2013. She won the Juno for Breakthrough Artist in 2005, and Let It Die in 2004 and The Reminder in 2007 came before Metals in 2011, which won the 2012 Polaris Music Prize. Pleasure followed in 2017 and Multitudes in 2023, and in summer 2026 she played outdoor dates at Red Rocks and Brookside Park in Pasadena.
artist_reel_line: In summer 2026 she played Red Rocks and Brookside Park in Pasadena.

intro: A deadpan post-punk band as their breakout accelerated.
story: Parquet Courts, a Brooklyn band by way of Denton, Texas, tore through Pickathon in 2013 with wired, deadpan post-punk energy, just as the acclaim for Light Up Gold was building, and they came back in 2014, the year of Sunbathing Animal. Human Performance, in 2016, had packaging nominated for a Grammy, and Wide Awake! followed in 2018 and Sympathy for Life in 2021. Andrew Savage's new band, Iconic Fugues, announced 2027 European dates.
artist_reel_line: Andrew Savage's new band, Iconic Fugues, announced 2027 European dates.
